title: Successor state preparation
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let the base configuration be a four-tape configuration on input $x$, and let $T$ be a table of the form $l\,1^u\,0\,r$, where $u$ is the unary size of an optional successor state: it is $0$ if there is no successor, and $q+1$ if the successor has index $q$. For any eight-bit action register and any such optional successor, starting in the successor-decoding phase with table cursor $|l|$, the unary tape encoding of state $0$, and state cursor $1$, after exactly $1$ steps if the successor is absent or $2q+4$ steps if its index is $q$, the interpreter is in the record-application phase with the same action register, a flag indicating whether the successor is absent, table cursor $|l|+u$, the unary encoding of state $0$ if absent or state $q$ otherwise, and state cursor $1$; all other configuration data are inherited from the base configuration.
hypotheses_covered: The base configuration is a four-tape configuration on input $x$
The successor is absent or is an index $q$ in the specified finite range
The table’s unary field length is $u=0$ when absent and $u=q+1$ when present
The action register is a function from the eight field indices to bits
replaced:
Suppose the table is $l \cdot 1^u \cdot 0 \cdot r$, where $u$ is the unary
size of an optional successor state ($0$ when the successor is absent and
$q + 1$ when it has index $q$).  From the interpreter's successor-decoding
phase carrying eight buffered action bits, with table cursor $|l|$, state
tape the intact unary encoding of the index $0$, and state cursor $1$,
exactly the successor-preparation cost ($1$ when the successor is absent
and $2q + 4$ otherwise) in interpreter steps reaches the record-application
phase carrying the same bits and a flag recording whether the successor is
absent, with table cursor $|l| + u$, state tape the intact unary encoding
of the successor index ($0$ when absent), and state cursor $1$.
